title: Count Out-Of-Sync Orders By Direction
description:
Report how many orders are out of sync **in each direction** between `source_orders` and `warehouse_orders`: how many exist only in source, and how many exist only in the warehouse.

Name the columns `direction` (`source_only` or `warehouse_only`) and `n`. Return exactly two rows, in any order.
hint: Use UNION ALL here, not UNION — you want exactly one row per direction even if both counts happen to be equal (UNION would collapse them into one row).
outputExplanation: Two orders (3, 4) are source-only and one order (5) is warehouse-only.

tests.name: Example
All three systems fully agree
Completely disjoint across all three
Source has an accidental duplicate row
Only source has any data
tests.seedSql: INSERT INTO source_orders VALUES (1,'Ann Lee',120.0),(2,'Ben Kim',80.0),(3,'Cy Ortiz',45.5);

tests.name: Same order, inconsistent name formatting
Matching ids, mismatched amounts
Single matching order everywhere
Larger mixed set: some in all three, some in two, some in one, duplicates and a mismatch
All synced — both counts are zero
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO source_orders VALUES (1,'A',100.0),(2,'B',200.0);
INSERT INTO warehouse_orders VALUES (1,'A',100.0),(2,'B',200.0);

tests.name: Completely disjoint — both directions non-zero
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO source_orders VALUES (1,'A',100.0),(2,'B',200.0);
INSERT INTO warehouse_orders VALUES (3,'C',300.0),(4,'D',400.0);

tests.name: Partial overlap
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO source_orders VALUES (1,'A',100.0),(2,'B',200.0),(3,'C',300.0);
INSERT INTO warehouse_orders VALUES (2,'B',200.0),(4,'D',400.0);
